outcome: Admissions to intensive or intermediate neonatal care
cohort: A sample of low-income Ecuadorian women with singleton pregnancies complicated by preeclampsia (mild or severe) or eclampsia, delivering at the Enrique C. Sotomayor Obstetrics and Gynecology Hospital.
finding: In this specific low-income Ecuadorian population, pregnancies complicated with severe preeclampsia/eclampsia resulted in adverse perinatal outcomes, including lower Apgar scores, more preterm births, and more low birth weight and small for gestational age infants, compared to mild preeclampsia.
mod_finding: Severe preeclampsia/eclampsia cases displayed a higher Caesarean-section rate.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from women delivering at the Enrique C. Sotomayor Obstetrics and Gynecology Hospital, focusing on outcomes at or immediately after birth.
